properties.name: A server holding several designs lists the ones under its root, as data
properties.statement:
A reflow2 server serving a registry root (`/g/<graph_id>/`) answers "which designs are here?" as structured data: each design's graph_id and label, enough for a caller to tell them apart. It lists exactly the designs under THAT root and nothing else, so the root stays the tenant boundary (dec:the-registry-root-is-the-tenant-boundary): no filtering by caller, and no identity system in reflow2.

Why: flo2's connector must answer "what designs do I have?" from chat (flo2 req:a-person-can-see-which-designs-they-have-from-chat, @ajs 2026-09-23), and flo2 keeps one registry root per person. Today reflow2 knows the list (Registry::graph_ids) but says it only inside the 404 text for an unaddressed request. The alternative, flo2's gateway reading the droplet's folders itself, was rejected by @ajs on 2026-09-23 because it re-implements what reflow2 already computes, which the dev_reflow2 hub trial measured drifting quietly.
